Intermediate labels around recent failures test whether retraining learned appropriate curves rather than merely correcting endpoints. The new pyridyl ketone, sulfur aldehyde, diketone, and aromatic alcohols test structural relationships that could transfer across many rows. Supplied CW distances and quantile widths were considered as secondary evidence; quantile spans are neither calibrated epistemic uncertainty nor elution interval widths.
